title: candidate feedback draft - Ethan Hu
content:
Interview notes (quick personal draft)

Role: Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
Interviewers: Sophie Chen (hiring manager), Lena Martinez (system design), Aaron Brooks (backend)
Date: 2026-03-18

High-level impression:
- Strong candidate overall. Deep systems background, very comfortable with distributed systems and GPU infra tradeoffs.
- Clear communicator, gave concrete examples from previous roles (scaling model serving, cache invalidation, rollout strategies).
- Some gaps around Rust/modern C++ low-level optimizations; mostly strong in Go/Python and system design.

Strengths:
- Distributed systems: designed and operated a multi-region model serving platform at previous company; explained autoscaling and circuit-breaker strategies well.
- Performance debugging: good story about tracing token-level latency regressions and isolating hot-paths (KV cache misses + kernel selection issues).
- Product sense: thought through fallback policies and rollback safety for canary rollouts; cares about safety of production rollouts.

Concerns / areas to probe further:
- Low-level runtime engineering (memory management, allocator choices) — less hands-on experience with C++/Rust kernels; prefers contributing at service/orchestration layer.
- Quantization/FP-specific experience seemed limited; has high-level familiarity but not deep experience running quantized kernels in-prod.
- Ownership bandwidth: previous role was smaller team; need to evaluate ability to drive cross-team projects at Redwood scale.

Scorecard (1-5):
- System design: 5
- Debugging/operational maturity: 4
- Low-level runtime / kernel dev: 3
- Collaboration / communication: 5
- Product sense / tradeoffs: 4

Recommendation:
- Strong hire for infra/service-focused role (serving runtime orchestration, routing, autoscaling). Would pair well with an engineer focused on kernel/runtime optimization. Recommend moving to final onsite (or small follow-up with kernel lead if we want to explicitly probe low-level runtime skills).

Follow-ups / interview asks (if next loop):
- Give a concrete debugging walkthrough: we should ask them to step through a hypothetical production regression where end-to-end latency spikes for short sequences — want to see how they'd use metrics/traces, KV cache checks, batching config, and kernel fallback to root cause and mitigation.
- Small take-home or design prompt around memory/kv cache management under multi-tenant workloads (optional).

Notes to self:
- Candidate is enthusiastic about Redwood's mission and asks good Qs about rollout policies and cost controls — flagged as culturally aligned.
- Consider pairing with infra lead (Aaron) for final calibration on ownership expectations and with our kernel lead (TBD) for a 30-min technical deep-dive if team wants explicit kernel evidence.

Unresolved:
- Confirm comp expectations and notice period (asked but candidate said she needs to confirm with current employer).

End of draft. Will refine after calibration chat with Lena + Aaron.
